budget_items.what_was_said: The board discussed renewing the yearly audit contract with Mark Bueller CPA, noting the fee went up from the prior year. Members said the contract is worthwhile because there are few small firms still doing this work and the auditor knows the district's routine.
Lancaster wells came back with elevated PFAS levels, requiring another round of sampling; if results stay high the district may have to move to monthly testing of all sources.

budget_items.topic: Keings PFAS treatment vs. Townsend interconnection
budget_items.what_was_said: Commissioners compared treating the Keings well for PFAS against building a pipe interconnection with Townsend, weighing the cost difference against the cost of also needing to buy water.

A commissioner asked whether a resident had been told the district previously lost SRF principal forgiveness funding, and noted new state PFAS funding announced by the Governor may include future principal forgiveness.
The board discussed renting a 30,000lb excavator to do main replacement work themselves instead of paying an engineer and contractor, comparing rental cost to the cost of hiring engineering design.
A commissioner recalled the town had bought a 16-inch road saw for a reasonable price and suggested the district consider buying one to make main-replacement jobs easier.

decisions.decision: Board agreed scenario 7 (intermunicipal connection to Townsend) should not stand alone in the survey; its cost should instead be added as a redundancy line item to scenarios 4/5 (Keings treatment).
Board agreed to send out the treatment-options survey largely as drafted, with a request to make clearer that a cheap option still requires a second phase/redundancy cost later.
Chair will send the draft survey to a resident (Bobby Turkington) and to Nicole for review before next meeting, aiming to present a final draft then.

minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Water District Commissioners approved minutes and renewed the CPA's yearly audit contract, then spent most of the meeting reworking a draft public survey on PFAS water-treatment options, debating scenarios ranging from treating the Keings well to interconnecting with Townsend or relying on Lancaster/Hickory Hills sources. They agreed to fold redundancy/interconnection costs into the treatment scenarios rather than list a standalone option, and to send the survey out largely as drafted after a couple more reviews. The board also covered new elevated PFAS results at Lancaster wells possibly triggering monthly testing, and operational items including main-replacement equipment, excavator rental, and a road saw purchase.

what_happened.line: Commissioners agreed to send residents a survey on PFAS water-treatment options, folding a Townsend interconnection into the treatment-scenario costs rather than listing it separately.
The board plans to send the survey largely as drafted, after review by a resident and by Nicole, with a final draft expected at the next meeting.
New PFAS test results at Lancaster wells came back elevated, which may push the district toward monthly testing of all its water sources.
The board voted to renew its yearly audit contract with the CPA firm, Mark Bueller, at a higher fee than the prior year.
Commissioners discussed renting an excavator to do main-replacement work themselves, and considered buying a road saw, instead of hiring outside engineering and contracting.

why_it_matters: The PFAS survey is how residents will be asked to weigh in on treatment options that carry multimillion-dollar price tags and could affect future water rates.
Elevated PFAS readings at Lancaster wells could trigger more frequent required testing, which is a cost and compliance issue for the district.
Equipment decisions like an excavator rental or a road saw purchase are being framed as ways to avoid paying outside engineers and contractors for main-replacement work.
